public_rationale: MiniMax's filing supports the narrower concern about operating cash outflows. It also reports positive gross margins. limitations: Company losses, gross margins and product profitability answer different questions.
The contract's press-estimate basis and combined scope cannot be replaced silently with one company's IFRS results.
Negative operating cash flow does not itself mean a company cannot pay bills using financing or cash reserves.

Unprofitable products means losses after attributable costs. Positive gross margins alone do not establish full product profitability, and company losses do not establish losses on every product.
Cashflow means internally generated operating cash, excluding new financing and previously raised cash reserves.

Bad margins has no objective cutoff; the universal profitability and operating-cash assertions remain testable.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence identifies a profitable covered product or a covered company whose internally generated operating cash covers its operating bills.
